title: Positive tangent weights give affine-space coordinates over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:\mathbf G_{m,k}\times_k X\to X$ be an algebraic action [def-sc-gm-ga], meaning a morphism satisfying $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $x\in X(k)$ be fixed as a morphism: $a(t,x)=x$ after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Let $T_xX$ be its relative tangent space [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Assume the differentiated action decomposes $T_xX$ as a direct sum of character spaces on which $t$ acts by $t^{n_i}$ with integers $n_i>0$. These are algebraic characters, not their differentials, and the direct sum may be empty. Put $d=\dim_kT_xX$. There is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes $X\simeq\mathbf A_k^d$ carrying $x$ to the origin, where $\mathbf A_k^d=\operatorname{Spec}k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. In particular if $d=0$, $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. The isomorphism is defined over $k$; no assumption that $k$ is algebraically closed, infinite or perfect is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 13.41 and Definition 13.40, printed pp.269-270; existence of Luna maps in Section 13e, pp.267-268. Only the genuinely strictly positive one-parameter case is used; no inference from absence of zero weights to positivity is asserted.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $\epsilon:A\to k$ be evaluation at the rational point $x$, with $\mathfrak m=\ker\epsilon$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $X$ is regular, including locally Noetherian. Geometric connectedness implies connectedness over $k$, and $x$ ensures nonemptiness. Thus [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $X$ integral; by [def-pc-integral-scheme], its nonempty affine chart $X$ has domain $A$. Set $R=A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The stalk identification in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] identifies $R$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$; it is therefore Noetherian regular local, with residue field $k$.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, irreducible case; smoothness everywhere permits the existing regular-connected-integral criterion, avoiding the reducible-case argument on p.270.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gm-affine-action-grading] over $k$ to obtain $A=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbf Z}A_q$, with pullback of a weight-$q$ function equal to $z^q$ times that function. Scheme-theoretic fixedness of $x$ says $\epsilon(f)z^q=\epsilon(f)$ for $f\in A_q$, as an identity in $k[z,z^{-1}]$. Uniqueness of Laurent coefficients gives $\epsilon(f)=0$ if $q\ne0$, even over a finite field. For $f=\sum_q f_q$, consequently $\epsilon(f)=\epsilon(f_0)$. Hence $\mathfrak m$ is homogeneous, $A_q=\mathfrak m\cap A_q$ for $q\ne0$, and $A_0=k\cdot1\oplus(\mathfrak m\cap A_0)$. Each $\mathfrak m^j$ is homogeneous, by expanding the factors of its generators into homogeneous parts. All quotients $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ therefore inherit these gradings.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269: A and m have weight decompositions and A_s=m_s for nonzero s; Stacks 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm), 0EKJ (example-Gm-on-affine), with universal Laurent parameter instead of k-points.

proof.text: The map $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, $u\mapsto u/1$, is an isomorphism. Indeed, for $s\notin\mathfrak m$ set $c=\epsilon(s)\in k^\times$. For $u\in\mathfrak m$, $u/s-c^{-1}u/1=u(c-s)/(cs)\in\mathfrak n^2$, proving surjectivity. If $u/1\in\mathfrak n^2$, the fraction equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $su\in\mathfrak m^2$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak m$. Since $(s-\epsilon(s))u\in\mathfrak m^2$, we get $\epsilon(s)u\in\mathfrak m^2$, hence $u\in\mathfrak m^2$. This proves injectivity. This canonical map commutes with pullback of functions fixing $x$, since both composites send $u$ to its pulled-back germ. In particular the induced weight decompositions agree. The vector space $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is finite dimensional: if $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ generate $A$ over $k$, polynomial subtraction of the constant term expresses every element of $\mathfrak m$ in the ideal generated by $g_i-\epsilon(g_i)$, whose classes consequently span $V$.

source.place: Section 13e, Lemmas 13.35--13.36, pp.267--268, identifying the affine and local cotangent spaces; explicit fraction calculation. Stacks 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: Use the natural duality [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] and step 3 to identify $T_xX$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(V,k)$. The operator on this dual space induced by $a_t$ sends $\lambda$ to $\lambda\circ a_t^*$, where $a_t^*$ is pullback on $V$. Thus its matrix is the transpose of the matrix of $a_t^*$, with no inverse. Explicitly, a tangent vector $v$ corresponds to $f\mapsto\epsilon(f)+\lambda_v([f-\epsilon(f)])\delta$ in $k[\delta]/(\delta^2)$; applying $a_t$ replaces $\lambda_v$ by $\lambda_v\circ a_t^*$. Take a tangent eigenbasis $v_i$ of characters $t^{n_i}$, $n_i>0$, and its dual basis $u_i$ in $V$. Then $\lambda_{v_j}(a_t^*u_i)=t^{n_j}\lambda_{v_j}(u_i)$ gives $a_t^*u_i=t^{n_i}u_i$. These are identities for the algebraic action: the same dual-number calculation over the universal coefficient ring $k[z,z^{-1}]$ reads the coaction coefficientwise. It does not test only $k^\times$. Consequently $V$ has only strictly positive graded degrees and $\dim_kV=d$. Choose homogeneous lifts $b_i\in\mathfrak m$ of the $u_i$, by taking the degree-$n_i$ component of any lift.

source.place: Lemmas 13.35--13.36 and Example 13.37, pp.267--268: cotangent lifts and equality of tangent weights with function-pullback weights. The inverse-free transpose calculation fixes the convention explicitly; Stacks 0B2E, lemma-tangent-space-rational-point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to the Noetherian local ring $R$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ and its rank-one module $R$. The maximal ideal is its Jacobson radical because it is the only maximal ideal, and the module is generated by $1$. Thus $\bigcap_{j\ge0}\mathfrak n^j=0$. If $f\in\bigcap_{j\ge0}\mathfrak m^j$, its image in $R$ belongs to every $\mathfrak n^j$, hence is zero. The map $A\to R$ is injective: by the fraction criterion [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $f/1=0$ implies $sf=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak m$; such an $s$ is nonzero, and $A$ is a domain. Therefore $\bigcap_{j\ge0}\mathfrak m^j=0$ in $A$ itself.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269, Krull-intersection argument in the irreducible case; Stacks 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, part (2).

proof.text: For $j\ge1$, products of $j$ classes in $V$ span $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ over $k$: write an element of $\mathfrak m^j$ as a finite sum $c\,h_1\cdots h_j$, $h_i\in\mathfrak m$; modulo $\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ replace $c$ by $\epsilon(c)$ and each $h_i$ by its linear combination of the $b_i$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$. Every resulting product has degree a sum of $j$ strictly positive integers. Hence these graded quotients have no components of degree $q\le0$. Now let $f\in\mathfrak m\cap A_q$ with $q\le0$. Starting with $f\in\mathfrak m$, if $f\in\mathfrak m^j$, its homogeneous class in $\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ must vanish, so $f\in\mathfrak m^{j+1}$. Induction and step 5 force $f=0$. Step 2 then gives $A_q=0$ for $q<0$ and $A_0=k\cdot1$. Thus the original grading is an $\mathbf N$-grading and $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{q>0}A_q$. This includes the empty tangent basis: the same product expansion makes every positive-adic quotient zero.

source.place: Theorem 13.41, p.269: products of cotangent lifts span each adic quotient, and separatedness detects the weight of each nonzero homogeneous function; written as induction to include the empty basis.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial] now hold for $F=k$, $B=A$: finite generation is step 1, $A_0=k$ and nonnegative grading are step 6, regularity of $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is step 1, and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ are homogeneous lifts of a basis by step 4. It follows that evaluation $k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$, $T_i\mapsto b_i$, is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. Taking spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] yields $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k[T_1,\ldots,T_d]=\mathbf A_k^d$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Because $b_i\in\ker\epsilon$, the composite evaluation to $k$ sends every $T_i$ to zero; this is precisely that $x$ maps to the origin. For $d=0$, the cited polynomial theorem gives $A=k$ and hence $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. All constructions and lifts were over $k$, with no scalar extension or descent of a chosen geometric isomorphism.

No new nodes, no statement change, no fixes. Step 1: affine finite type gives a finitely generated algebra; smooth gives regular; geometrically connected plus the point x gives nonempty and connected, so integral and A is a domain; A_m = O_{X,x}. Step 2: the grading lemma with the universal Laurent parameter makes m homogeneous and nonzero weights lie in m, also for finite k. Step 3: m/m^2 = n/n^2, surjectivity and injectivity verified by hand. Step 4: the tangent operator is the transpose of a_t^*, so the weights have the same sign (checked on A^1 with weight 2); the computation is done over k[z^{±1}], so algebraic characters are detected, including weight p in characteristic p. Step 5: Krull intersection is applied in the local ring R (Jacobson hypothesis holds there), then pulled back to A because A is a domain; this matches Milne. Step 6: the spanning argument and the induction give A_0 = k, A_q = 0 for q < 0, and handle d = 0. Step 7: every hypothesis of lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial checked; Spec and A^d_k give the isomorphism, and x goes to the origin. Edge cases tested: Spec k, weights (2,5), finite k, weight p in char p. No duplicate: the luna-coordinates, equivariant-inverse and cotangent-lifts nodes are over algebraically closed fields only, and the unipotence node needs this item over arbitrary k. The four declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch 5: lem-trf-polynomial-nonzero-ideal-quotient-dimension-bound (dim k[t]/I <= n-1 for nonzero I) is pure commutative algebra and part of neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality, so the citation through positive-graded-regular-polynomial is acceptable.
